other.detail: Iteration 5 showed that the isResolved() guard is behaviour-bearing: tests failed when it was removed. Iteration 12 showed that dereferencing a map result guarded only by a throw-only helper triggers an SFGE ApexNullPointerException. Iteration 10 failed to compile because a new private field was placed directly under @NamespaceAccessible.

other.title: Headroom gains are near the noise floor
other.detail: Iterations 7 and 8 were kept on the overall margin while their focus gain (5.0 and 4.4) was below the 5-point margin, after re-measuring. Their headroom benefit is real but modest and may not reproduce.

retro.head: 09db986516bfe2a30138085d654f269ce476aee8
retro.summary: Only fflib_SecurityUtils changed, so it drove every score change. Graph Engine went from 67.6 to 100 in iteration 2, which swapped fflib_SObjectDescribe.getField for the native Schema field map. Limit headroom went from 52.3 to 100 in iteration 4, which added a per-user cache of field names that already passed. Resource efficiency and Test run time barely moved, and fflib_QueryFactoryTest fell slightly (80.9 to 80.3). The main risk: iteration 2 dropped getField's handling of relationship names and namespace prefixes, so names like 'Account' or 'Foo__r' now cause a NullPointerException, and the iteration 4 cache can keep a pass after a permission is revoked in the same transaction for the same user.

behaviourChanges.title: Relationship-style field names are no longer resolved
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline fflib_SObjectDescribe.getField mapped 'X__r' to 'X__c', 'X__pr' to 'X__pc' and a standard lookup name such as 'Account' to 'AccountId'. The native fields.getMap().get() does none of this, so it returns null and the SObjectField overload throws System.NullPointerException instead of running the FLS check. This affects checkInsert, checkRead and checkUpdate with List<String>, and the three single-field String overloads. All are public @NamespaceAccessible API.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: As an admin, call checkRead(Contact.SObjectType, new List<String>{'Account'}) and checkFieldIsReadable(Contact.SObjectType, 'Account'). Assert that no exception is thrown, which matches the baseline.

behaviourChanges.title: Namespace prefix is no longer added to field names
behaviourChanges.detail: The baseline called getField(name, true), which tried the package namespace prefix. The native describe map is used as it is, and whether it finds unprefixed custom field names inside a managed package is not verified. If it does not, those lookups return null and throw a NullPointerException.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In a namespaced packaging org, call checkRead(SomeObj__c.SObjectType, new List<String>{'Field__c'}) without the prefix and assert it gives the same result as the prefixed name.

behaviourChanges.title: Cached passes can outlive a permission revocation in the same transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: verifiedFieldNames remembers names that passed, keyed by operation and SObjectType, and clears only when UserInfo.getUserId() changes. If a permission set assignment is removed later in the transaction, or a test runs two System.runAs blocks for the same user with permissions changed between them, a later List<String> check for cached names skips the per-field FLS check and passes without checking. The object CRUD check still runs on every call.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: As user U with a permission set granting read on a custom field, call checkRead and see it pass. Delete the PermissionSetAssignment, run as U again and call checkRead with the same list. Assert it throws FlsException.

behaviourChanges.title: Fields that fflib_SObjectDescribe resolved to null are now checked
behaviourChanges.detail: Some fields, such as Opportunity.LastSyncTime, resolve to null through fflib_SObjectDescribe.getField, so the baseline threw a NullPointerException on them. The native map finds them and runs a real FLS check. This changes behaviour in a good direction.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call checkRead(Opportunity.SObjectType, new List<String>{'LastSyncTime'}) as an admin and assert that it does not throw.

patterns.title: Replacing a library wrapper with the native API to clear an analyzer warning
patterns.detail: This removed the call that could return null, but it also dropped real behaviour: relationship-name and namespace handling. The analyzer score went up while the API contract got narrower.

patterns.title: Fetching the field map once per call
patterns.detail: Fetching the map once before the loop instead of once per field is a sound saving.

patterns.title: Static cache of security results that passed
patterns.detail: It stores only after success with bypass off and resets when the user changes, which is careful. Its weak points are permission changes within a transaction, a String key rather than typed maps, and case-sensitive names (a cache miss only, not a correctness issue). It covers only the List<String> overloads, so behaviour differs from the List<SObjectField> and single-field overloads.

patterns.title: No caching on the single-token path
patterns.detail: Iteration 7 was rejected after it gained nothing and cost coverage, so the paths QueryFactory uses stay without a cache.

testGaps.title: Relationship and __r/__pr field names
testGaps.detail: No test passes a relationship-style name to the String overloads.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that checkRead, checkInsert and checkUpdate, plus checkFieldIs* with String, accept 'Account' on Contact and 'Parent' on Account without throwing for an admin.

testGaps.title: Cache staleness for the same user
testGaps.detail: The tests check a cache reset only through a change of user ID.
testGaps.proposedTest: Check, revoke a permission set for the same user, check again, and expect FlsException.

testGaps.title: Cache does not hide a field that failed
testGaps.detail: No test covers a list that partly overlaps a cached set and contains a field that is not allowed.
testGaps.proposedTest: As a read-only user, call checkRead with readable fields, then call it with those fields plus one unreadable field. Expect FlsException on the second call.

testGaps.title: Bypass does not fill the cache
testGaps.detail: Nothing asserts that a pass under BYPASS leaves no cache entry behind.
testGaps.proposedTest: As a read-only user, set BYPASS=true and call checkUpdate. Then set BYPASS=false, call checkUpdate with the same list and expect CrudException or FlsException.

testGaps.title: Unknown or null field names
testGaps.detail: The exception type for a field name that cannot be resolved is not pinned down.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that checkRead(Account.SObjectType, new List<String>{'NoSuchField'}) throws System.NullPointerException, or decide that it should throw SecurityException and change the code.

other.title: Small runtime gains for the default callers
other.detail: QueryFactory and SObjectSelector call the SObjectField and single-String overloads, and in legacy FLS mode only. They gain nothing from the cache, which explains why Resource efficiency barely moved. The single-String overloads now call getDescribe().fields.getMap() on every call, which may cost more than the fflib_SObjectDescribe instance cache they replaced, for example at fflib_QueryFactory.cls:777.

other.title: The headroom test hides the relationship-name loss
other.detail: The headroom test builds its lists from canonical describe names and skips fields that getField cannot resolve, so the test data never contains the name forms the baseline was there to handle.

retro.head: 04e420b28542d951ff3881d31a07f1e0ee6655a0
retro.summary: Only iteration 1 was kept. It turned 15 indexed loops in fflib_SObjects.cls into for-each loops and made the constructor's describe DEFERRED, which took PMD from 42.4 to 100 with no suppressions. Limit headroom (-1.0) and Resource efficiency (-1.0) fell slightly, within noise, so the expected CPU gain did not happen. Iterations 2-4 targeted CPU, none beat its noise margin, and all were discarded. Behaviour is unchanged on every tested path; the remaining differences are edge cases no test runs: a list modified during a loop, and the deferred describe exposed through a public property.

behaviourChanges.title: For-each loops throw if the record list is modified during iteration
behaviourChanges.detail: The old loops cached the size in j and read records[i], so if a callee added to or removed from the list behind getRecords() mid-loop, the loop still finished (it skipped appended items or failed with an out-of-bounds error on removal). Apex for-each throws System.FinalException 'Cannot modify a collection while it is being iterated' instead. Library code never mutates the list inside these loops. A subclass could, though: it can override getRecords() to return a shared list, or override the virtual hooks such as error() or the addError overloads to touch domain records. Element order and null elements behave the same as before.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In fflib_SObjectsTest, write a subclass whose getRecords() returns a shared list and whose error() override appends a record to that list. Call addError('x') and assert the outcome you want (either an explicit FinalException or a successful finish), so this behaviour is pinned down.

behaviourChanges.title: Public sObjectDescribe now holds a deferred DescribeSObjectResult
behaviourChanges.detail: sObjectDescribe is a public @NamespaceAccessible property, and it now holds a result created with SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED. Child relationships load on first access instead of up front. Subscribers and subclasses that call getChildRelationships() still get the same data, but the describe cost moves to that first call. Identity or equality comparisons against a default getDescribe() result are not guaranteed to hold. Inside the repo, only fflib_SObjectDomain reads it (isCreateable/isUpdateable/isDeletable/isUndeletable/getName at fflib_SObjectDomain.cls:252-299) plus getSObjectType(), and none of these depend on the option.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Construct fflib_SObjects(new List<Account>(), Account.SObjectType) and assert that sObjectDescribe.getChildRelationships() is non-empty and matches Account.SObjectType.getDescribe().getChildRelationships().size(). Also assert that getSObjectType() == Account.SObjectType.

patterns.title: Indexed loops with comma declarations replaced by for-each
patterns.detail: Cleaner and idiomatic. It clears OneDeclarationPerLine without suppressions. The loop variable names (record/current) match the old locals, which keeps the diff minimal.

patterns.title: DEFERRED describe in the domain constructor
patterns.detail: It clears EagerlyLoadedDescribeSObjectResult and costs nothing on the paths the library uses. It did not lower CPU, and iteration 4 found the describe call is already cheap.

patterns.title: Discarding the micro-optimisations
patterns.detail: Iterations 2 and 3 would have added null short-circuits, Set-to-List copies, and a get-then-containsKey rewrite of setFieldValueByMap. Iteration 4 would have added a lazy describe property and a duplicate state field. Each added complexity or a subtle change to null handling for no measured gain, and discarding them kept the class simpler.

testGaps.title: CRUD-denied paths of fflib_SObjectDomain on the deferred describe
testGaps.detail: The trigger CRUD checks read SObjectDescribe.isCreateable()/getName() and so on. It is not clear the tests cover the denied branch as a user without object permission.
testGaps.proposedTest: Use System.runAs with a Minimum Access user and EnforcingTriggerCRUDSecurity enabled. Call handleBeforeInsert/Update/Delete/Undelete and assert a DomainException whose message contains the object name.

testGaps.title: Mutating the list during iteration
testGaps.detail: Nothing tests a callee that modifies the record list during addError, clearFields or setFieldValue.
testGaps.proposedTest: See the first behaviour change: a subclass whose override appends to the shared list during addError, with the expected outcome asserted.

testGaps.title: Null element in the records list
testGaps.detail: The old and new loops both throw NullPointerException on a null element, but no test pins this down.
testGaps.proposedTest: new fflib_SObjects(new List<Account>{ null }, Account.SObjectType).getIdFieldValues(Account.Id) should throw NullPointerException.

other.title: Baseline aggregate scores don't match the per-test values
other.detail: Each dimension has only one contributor, so the score should equal its per-test value. The baseline reports Limit headroom 57.3 against a per-test 59.8, and Resource efficiency 82.3 against a per-test 82.8. The evolved scores match their per-test values. This suggests the baseline aggregates come from a different run, which makes the reported deltas less reliable.

other.title: CPU in the headroom test is dominated by platform calls
other.detail: Iterations 2-4 found that the cost is in record.get/put/contains and in dispatch work, not in loop form or describe calls. Further headroom gains would mean making fewer calls or visiting fewer records, which the current API contract may not allow.

retro.head: e6e07dc1a50696d25696c85460302232e1e5d9ac
retro.summary: Only fflib_QueryFactory.cls changed, so it caused every score change: Graph Engine (iteration 3), PMD (iterations 10 and 12) and Limit headroom (iterations 5, 7 and 12, by memoizing field paths, tokens, names, child relationships and table names in NONE mode). Resource efficiency barely moved (+4.9, inside its 6.8 noise margin) because the selector path (fflib_SObjectSelectorTest) was never meaningfully improved. Iteration 12 was kept on overall score even though its focus, Limit headroom, rose only 5.1, under the 5.3 margin. For valid input, results match the baseline; the differences are in error types, locale edge cases, heap that lasts the whole transaction, and an equals/hashCode contract mismatch that is now explicit, and no test pins any of them down.

behaviourChanges.title: Ordering(String sobjType, ...) with an unknown or blank object name now throws InvalidFieldException instead of NullPointerException
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline dereferenced fflib_SObjectDescribe.getDescribe(sobjType).getField(...) directly, so an unknown or blank object name raised System.NullPointerException. Now getSObjectField returns null, and Ordering(SObjectField, SortOrder) passes it to getFieldTokenPath(null), which throws InvalidFieldException('Invalid field: null'). The message names neither the object nor the field. Callers that catch NullPointerException will behave differently. This is arguably an improvement, but it is a contract change.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Construct new fflib_QueryFactory.Ordering('NotAnObject__x', 'Name', SortOrder.ASCENDING) and assert that InvalidFieldException (and not NullPointerException) is thrown.

behaviourChanges.title: Explicit hashCode is identity-based while equals is based on SOQL
behaviourChanges.detail: hashCode returns a per-instance counter, but equals compares table, field count and toSOQL(). Two factories that are equal under equals() have different hashes, so Set.contains or Map.get with an equal but different instance misses. That breaks the Apex equals/hashCode contract. It matches the baseline's observed runtime behaviour (the deterministic_toSOQL Set kept two entries), but it now formally declares that equal objects hash differently, and the comment documents it as intended. Each instance also carries a new instanceId field, which appears in JSON.serialize and debug output and changes the class's serialized shape. The counter is a static, non-final Integer that grows across the transaction.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Build two factories with identical selects and assert qf1.equals(qf2). Then assert the intended Set/Map behaviour explicitly (for example new Set<fflib_QueryFactory>{qf1}.contains(qf2)), so the contract is pinned down in one direction or the other.

behaviourChanges.title: Static caches last the whole transaction and grow without bound
behaviourChanges.detail: Five static final maps (field tokens, field names, field paths keyed by the exact case-sensitive input string, child relationships per SObjectType, table names) are never cleared within a transaction. In a long transaction such as a batch execute, Queueable or big trigger that builds queries for many objects or with varied field-name casing, heap grows. For example, the full Account child-relationship map is held for the whole transaction. fflib_SObjectDescribe already caches describes, so this is a second layer of caching on top of it. Heap is not measured by any headroom test.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Headroom test that selects 200 fields in mixed case across 20 SObjectTypes and asserts that Limits.getHeapSize() growth stays below a budget.

behaviourChanges.title: Child-relationship lookup now uses the running user's locale through toLowerCase in a transaction-wide cache
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline compared names with Apex == (case-insensitive) on every call. Evolved lowercases both the key and the lookup with String.toLowerCase(), which follows the context user's locale. The map is built once per transaction. If the map is built under one locale (for example tr_TR, where 'I' lowercases to 'ı') and looked up after System.runAs switches to a user with another locale, a name containing 'I' (such as a custom 'Invoices__r') misses and throws InvalidSubqueryRelationshipException. Field tokens (getCachedField) have the same cross-runAs exposure, although baseline already lowercased field names on each call.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Inside System.runAs of a user whose LocaleSidKey is 'tr' (Turkish), call subselectQuery for a relationship whose name contains 'I', after the cache has been warmed by a call outside runAs, and assert the relationship resolves.

behaviourChanges.title: NONE-mode string selects bypass addField
behaviourChanges.detail: selectStringField in NONE mode calls fields.add directly instead of addField. That is equivalent today because addField only lowercases in USER_MODE and SYSTEM_MODE. Any future logic added to addField (validation, normalisation, sorting hooks) will silently skip NONE-mode string selects, while selectField(String, SObjectType), selectFieldSet and SObjectField selects still go through it.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Regression test that selects the same field through selectField('name'), selectFields(List) and selectFieldSet in NONE mode and asserts a single entry in getSelectedFields().

behaviourChanges.title: Invalid-field lookups now cache a null token
behaviourChanges.detail: getCachedField stores null for an unknown name (it checks containsKey), so later calls skip fflib_SObjectDescribe entirely. Exceptions are the same because the null token still reaches InvalidFieldException. This relies on describe results being fixed for the whole transaction, which holds in Apex.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Call selectField('NotAField__c') twice on Contact and assert that InvalidFieldException is thrown both times.

behaviourChanges.title: First call per object to subselectQuery(String) now scans and lowercases every child relationship
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline returned on the first match. Evolved builds the whole map on first use (about 100+ entries for Account) and is faster on repeat calls. A transaction that does a single subselect pays slightly more CPU.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: No functional test needed. Optionally add a single-subselect CPU headroom assertion.

patterns.title: Memoizing the final resolved path behind a thin wrapper, with the original method unchanged
patterns.detail: getFieldPath caches only when the result is user-independent (NONE mode, no related type) and otherwise delegates to the original resolveFieldPath. FLS checks (LEGACY) and the polymorphic branch are never cached. The design is correct and easy to reason about.

patterns.title: Several stacked cache layers that duplicate fflib_SObjectDescribe
patterns.detail: Field tokens, field names and field paths are cached at three levels, and fflib_SObjectDescribe has its own describe cache underneath. Iterations 6 and 8 showed that the extra layers bring almost no gain, yet the token and name layers from iteration 5 remain, and are now largely made redundant by the path memo for NONE mode.

patterns.title: Declaring caches static final to stay under PMD TooManyFields
patterns.detail: The caches are never reassigned, so final is semantically correct. However, the change was made to exploit a gap in the rule, not to fix the design. The class still holds many fields, and the caches would be better grouped in a small holder class.

patterns.title: Identity hashCode added to silence OverrideBothEqualsAndHashcode
patterns.detail: This clears the PMD finding by writing in a hashCode that is inconsistent with equals. The cleaner fix would be a documented suppression or removing equals. As written it misleads readers into thinking the pair is consistent.

patterns.title: Null-safe outer static helper for the inner-class constructor
patterns.detail: getSObjectField replaces a raw dereference with a clear failure path and satisfies Graph Engine. It is small and correct.

patterns.title: Splitting selectStringField by mode
patterns.detail: The duplicated loops and direct fields.add couple NONE mode to how addField behaves today.

testGaps.title: Ordering with an unknown SObject name
testGaps.detail: No test covers the null-describe path that iteration 3 changed.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that InvalidFieldException is thrown by new Ordering('Bogus__x', 'Name', SortOrder.ASCENDING).

testGaps.title: Case-insensitive subselect names and the null-name entry
testGaps.detail: The case-folding equivalence between the lowercased-key map and Apex == is not pinned down.
testGaps.proposedTest: On an Account factory, call subselectQuery('contacts') and subselectQuery('CONTACTS'), assert both resolve to the same relationship, and assert the generated SOQL uses the canonical 'Contacts'.

testGaps.title: Mixed FLS modes on the same table in one transaction
testGaps.detail: The cache is shared across factories. No test checks that a NONE factory warming the cache does not affect a later LEGACY factory's FLS check or a USER_MODE factory's lowercasing.
testGaps.proposedTest: Select 'Name' in NONE mode, then under System.runAs a user without FLS on a custom field, build a LEGACY factory selecting that field and assert that FLS exception is thrown. Also assert that USER_MODE selects are lowercase.

testGaps.title: Repeated invalid field
testGaps.detail: Null tokens are cached. No test checks that the second call still throws.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call selectField('Nope__c') twice in NONE mode and twice in LEGACY mode, and expect InvalidFieldException each time.

testGaps.title: Polymorphic path with and without a related type in the same transaction
testGaps.detail: The cache is bypassed when relatedSObjectType is non-null. No test confirms that a cached null-type result doesn't leak into a related-type call or the reverse.
testGaps.proposedTest: On Task, selectField('What.Name') first, then selectField('What.Name', Account.SObjectType), and assert both produce the expected path.

testGaps.title: equals/hashCode contract
testGaps.detail: The only coverage is indirect, through the Set in deterministic_toSOQL.
testGaps.proposedTest: Explicit assertions on qf1.equals(qf2), qf1.hashCode() != qf2.hashCode(), and Map<fflib_QueryFactory,...> lookup behaviour, so any future change is deliberate.

testGaps.title: Heap growth of the static caches
testGaps.detail: Limit headroom measures CPU only.
testGaps.proposedTest: Bulk test asserting a Limits.getHeapSize() delta budget after querying many objects and field casings.

other.title: Resource efficiency gain is noise
other.detail: +4.9 is within the 6.8 margin. fflib_SObjectSelector paths go through selectField(String, SObjectType) and SObjectField selects, which bypass the main path memo, so selector-heavy callers see little improvement.

other.title: Measurements were noisy
other.detail: Iteration 9's first run also measured Limit headroom at 90 and was discarded after averaging, while iteration 12 was kept on overall score. The final 90 may be partly variance, so re-measure before relying on it.

other.title: Iteration 10 comment is a borderline justification comment
other.detail: The hashCode comment explains intent that the contract violation makes necessary, but it reads more like a rationale belonging in the PR. Consider a PMD suppression with a short reason instead.

retro.head: 53ad240c34308d734bf1fa4182c79ddea2caeaf8
retro.summary: The only change kept was iteration 3: a static Map<SObjectType,String> cache (fflib_SObjectSelector.cls:117) that remembers the default ORDER BY, read before the original logic and written after it (cls:222-224, cls:239). The original name-field, encryption and CreatedDate/Id logic is unchanged, and Apex statics last only one transaction, so behaviour should be the same. fflib_SObjectSelector.cls is the only class changed and drove every score change. Limit headroom (+4.8) did not beat its 5.7 margin, and the headroom test's own score rose only 51.8 → 52.8, which doesn't match the dimension's 48.2 → 53. The coverage, run-time and resource-efficiency moves (ApplicationTest 80 → 81.9) look like noise.

behaviourChanges.title: Default order-by is now shared by all selector instances of the same SObjectType in a transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: Before, each instance worked out its default order-by from describe data. Now the first instance per type computes it and later instances, including other selector subclasses for the same type, reuse that string. This is only safe because the computed value depends only on the type: the name field, isEncrypted() and whether the type has CreatedDate are all org metadata. Statics reset per transaction, so nothing leaks between transactions. Subclasses that override getOrderBy() without calling super never touch the cache.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: In one test, create two different selector subclasses for the same type, one of which is an Account selector with the default getOrderBy(). Assert that both return the literal 'Name'. Do the same for CaseComment and assert the literal 'CreatedDate'.

behaviourChanges.title: Cached value carries across System.runAs user switches in the same transaction
behaviourChanges.detail: In tests, System.runAs does not reset statics, so a value computed as one user is reused as another. Today none of the inputs vary by user: describe getMap() returns fields regardless of FLS, and name field and encryption are metadata. If the order-by logic ever adds a per-user check such as isAccessible(), the cache would silently serve the first user's result.
behaviourChanges.evidence: fflib_SObjectSelector.cls:225-239; FLS tests around fflib_SObjectSelectorTest.cls:398-430 use runAs
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Inside a single test, compute getOrderBy() as an admin and then again inside System.runAs with a minimal-access user. Assert that both match what an uncached computation gives for that user.

behaviourChanges.title: getSObjectType() is called more often on a cache miss
behaviourChanges.detail: On a miss, getSObjectType() now runs 3 times instead of 1. On a hit it runs once and skips getNameField. This only matters if a subclass's getSObjectType() is expensive or has side effects, which would be unusual. A null type would behave as before: Map.get(null) is legal and the original code path then runs.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: None needed beyond the shared-instance test above.

patterns.title: Flat static per-type memoisation of a pure derived string
patterns.detail: The cache is cheap to look up, holds very little memory (one string per type), lasts only the transaction, and leaves the original logic untouched. That is why PMD and Graph Engine held at 100 (iterations 1 and 2 lost points by restructuring the code).

patterns.title: The same `if (m_orderBy == null)` check appears twice in a row
patterns.detail: Two adjacent identical checks look accidental and invite a later 'simplification' that merges them and breaks the cache-hit path. The score tools (PMD, Graph Engine) rewarded this shape, but people reading it may not see why. It would read better as a cache read followed by one guarded block, or a short early return.

patterns.title: Mutable static cache that is not final and not documented
patterns.detail: `private static Map<...> defaultOrderByCache` is reassignable and nothing marks it as a cache shared across instances. `static final` would be safer. This file already uses non-final statics for its constants (cls:115-116), so it is consistent with local style.

testGaps.title: Most order-by assertions derive the expected value from getOrderBy() itself
testGaps.detail: Tests at fflib_SObjectSelectorTest.cls:176, 308, 334, 454, 470, 883 and 925 build the expected SOQL from selector.getOrderBy(). A wrong cached value would match itself and pass. Only cls:208 ('Name' prefix) and cls:841 ('ORDER BY CreatedDate') check literal values, and each test method is a fresh transaction, so they mostly exercise the cache-miss path.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert literal defaults on both the miss and the hit path in one transaction: Account → 'Name', CaseComment → 'CreatedDate', and an object with neither a name field nor CreatedDate → 'Id'. Call each selector twice, plus a second subclass for the same type.

testGaps.title: Encrypted name field fallback
testGaps.detail: The isEncrypted() branch (cls:232) is not pinned by a literal assertion, so caching the wrong branch would go unnoticed.
testGaps.proposedTest: If the org has an object with an encrypted name field (or one can be set up), assert that getOrderBy() returns 'CreatedDate' or 'Id' on both calls. Otherwise record this as a known gap.

testGaps.title: Headroom test does not check results
testGaps.detail: headroomBulkSelectorQueries checks only totalLength > 0 and the row count, so the order-by text inside the 600 rounds of generated SOQL is never checked.
testGaps.proposedTest: After the loop, assert that new CaseSelector().newQueryFactory().toSOQL() ends with the expected literal 'ORDER BY <field> ASC NULLS FIRST '.

other.title: Headroom gain is within noise
other.detail: Iteration 3 was kept on overall score (+0.9 against a 0.8 margin) after re-measuring, while its focus dimension stayed below its margin. Iterations 4-6 show the remaining CPU is spread across many query-building paths, so more caching at this level has little left to gain. fflib_SObjectDescribe.getNameField is still uncached and loops over every field. Caching it there, per type, would help every caller, not just selectors.

other.title: Reported headroom numbers are inconsistent
other.detail: The dimension is said to be the mean of its per-test scores, yet it went 48.2 → 53 while its only test went 51.8 → 52.8. Check the scoring pipeline before trusting the size of the gain.

retro.head: bb6f9c750cb3583ef5eeae1755bfc02259ce9b65
retro.summary: Only fflib_SObjectDescribe.cls changed, so it drove every score: PMD 71.4→100 (iterations 1, 2, 4) and Limit headroom 64.8→72.7 (iteration 4, by memoizing the name-field scan on the cached instance). Resource efficiency barely moved (QueryFactory 81.3→80.9, SecurityUtils flat at 79), and run time and coverage changes are within noise. Iteration 4 deleted the DEFERRED describe that iterations 1-2 had added, so the PMD EagerlyLoadedDescribeSObjectResult finding cleared because the eager describe moved to line 48, which the rule does not flag, not because eager loading stopped. The static getNameField now also builds and caches a describe instance, which contradicts its own ApexDoc.

behaviourChanges.title: Static getNameField now creates and caches a describe instance with an eager full describe
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline: static getNameField(type) did a one-off native describe and kept no wrapper state. Evolved: it calls getDescribe(objectType), which builds an fflib_SObjectDescribe, stores it in instanceCache, and loads the full eager describe (line 48, no DEFERRED, so child relationships load) plus the field map. These stay in heap until flushCache(). fflib_SObjectSelector.cls:200 calls this, so every selector type now holds a cached wrapper. Net effect: the DEFERRED optimisation from iterations 1-2 is gone, and eager loading persists at line 48.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: After flushCache(), call getNameField(Account.SObjectType), then assert that getDescribe(Account.SObjectType) returns an instance and document whether that is intended. Separately, measure Limits.getHeapSize() before and after getNameField over many types.

behaviourChanges.title: Name field results now survive until flushCache and are tied to an instance
behaviourChanges.detail: The instance getNameField() used to recompute from token on every call. Now it is memoized on the instance and the static method reads the cached instance. A caller holding an instance across flushCache() keeps its old nameField. Schema does not change within a transaction, so practical impact is low, but this is a semantic shift from stateless to cached.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Assert that getNameField(Account.SObjectType) returns the same value as getDescribe(Account.SObjectType).getNameField() both before and after flushCache().

behaviourChanges.title: Types with no name field rescan every call
behaviourChanges.detail: nameField uses null to mean 'not computed', so a type whose fields all have isNameField()=false repeats the full per-field getDescribe() scan on every call. The cost is about the same as the baseline for those types, but the cache never helps them.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Find a standard object with no name field and assert that getNameField returns null on repeated calls, checking Limits.getCpuTime growth if needed.

behaviourChanges.title: String and DescribeSObjectResult lookups now share the token-keyed cache
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline getDescribe(String): on a cache miss under the given name, it constructed a new instance, even if the token was already cached under its real name. This happens with namespace-implied names such as 'Foo__c' resolving to ns__Foo__c, where the baseline built a new instance and overwrote the cache on every call. Evolved: it delegates to getDescribe(token), which reuses the instance cached under String.valueOf(token). The DescribeSObjectResult overload switched its cache key from getName() to String.valueOf(token), which is the same in practice. This is an improvement, but instance identity changes for namespaced callers. The non-null DescribeSObjectResult and SObject paths are untested; their asserts are commented out at test lines 156-162.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Uncomment the d4 and d5 asserts in getAccountDescribes. Add a test that sets currentNamespace and asserts that getDescribe('Foo__c') === getDescribe('ns__Foo__c').

behaviourChanges.title: Index loops rewritten as for-each loops
behaviourChanges.detail: getNameField scan, getPicklistLabels and isValidPicklistValue now use for-each loops. Iteration order and the behaviour on null lists (exception in both versions) are the same.

patterns.title: Fixing PMD by matching the rule's text
patterns.detail: Iteration 2 renamed a parameter and dropped the Schema. prefix to get past the rule's text matching. Iteration 4 then sent the call through the unflagged line 48. The score reached 100 while the eager describe the rule targets is still there.

patterns.title: Memoizing the name field on the cached per-type instance
patterns.detail: Reuses the existing instanceCache and flushCache lifecycle, adds no new static map, and removed the dominant CPU cost. It needs a sentinel for 'no name field', and the docs need updating.

patterns.title: Collapsing overloads into delegation to getDescribe(SObjectType)
patterns.detail: One code path, fewer branches, and the cache behaviour is consistent across overloads.

patterns.title: Stale documentation left behind
patterns.detail: The @deprecated note on the instance getNameField says the static method works 'without requiring a describe instance', which is now false: the deprecated instance method is the underlying implementation. The test comment at line 210 says the instance method delegates to the static one; the reverse is now true.

patterns.title: Trading lint complexity budget for features
patterns.detail: Iteration 4 removed branches elsewhere to stay under PMD's class complexity threshold. The result here was fine, but the climb chose refactors for score budget rather than design.

testGaps.title: Non-null DescribeSObjectResult and SObject overloads
testGaps.detail: The cache-identity asserts are commented out, so the iteration 4 delegation is checked only for nulls.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert that getDescribe(Account.SObjectType.getDescribe()) === getDescribe('Account') and getDescribe(new Account()) === getDescribe('Account').

testGaps.title: Static and instance getNameField agree, including after flush
testGaps.detail: Nothing checks that the two methods share state or behave the same after flushCache.
testGaps.proposedTest: For Account, Contact and Case, assert static == instance getNameField, call flushCache(), then assert again and compare to a direct scan of type.getDescribe().fields.getMap().

testGaps.title: Type without a name field
testGaps.detail: The null result and its repeated rescans are not exercised.
testGaps.proposedTest: Pick a standard object with no isNameField field and assert getNameField returns null on two consecutive calls.

testGaps.title: Namespace-implied String lookup reuses the cache
testGaps.detail: The new cache sharing for implied-namespace names is untested.
testGaps.proposedTest: With a fake currentNamespace, as in the existing namespace test, assert that getDescribe by the short name and by the full name return the same instance.

testGaps.title: Heap and describe cost of selector name-field resolution
testGaps.detail: fflib_SObjectSelector now caches a full eager wrapper per type. Nothing measures this.
testGaps.proposedTest: A headroom test that builds selectors for about 50 types and asserts that heap and CPU stay within a budget.

other.title: Possible follow-up
other.detail: Use SObjectDescribeOptions.DEFERRED at line 48 to bring back the intent of iterations 1-2. Iteration 5 found this gave negligible headroom, but it is semantically honest. Also cache 'no name field' with a separate Boolean flag, and fix the ApexDoc at lines 142-143.

other.title: Headroom ceiling
other.detail: Iterations 5-7 show the remaining CPU goes to native describe calls and rebuilds after the test's deliberate flushCache calls. Further work on Apex-level helpers is unlikely to pass the 8.3 margin.

retro.head: d8b7c6da1c245a6ce17ce81781aa73e3a831b65b
retro.summary: Only iteration 1 was kept: it deleted two System.debug(INFO) developer hints from SelectorFactory.setMock(fflib_ISObjectSelector) and DomainFactory.setMock(fflib_ISObjectDomain) in fflib_Application.cls, which accounts for the whole PMD rise from 92.6 to 100. The Limit headroom rise (57.4 to 64.9) and Test run time rise (90.1 to 90.8) are measurement noise: headroomBulkFactoryCalls never calls setMock, so the deleted lines do not run there, and iterations 2 to 4 show headroom swinging by 2.5 to 6.5 points. Coverage stayed at 90.1 only because the scorer counts each multi-line statement as one line; at 107/119 it would be about 89.9. Functional behaviour is unchanged. The only loss is a diagnostic hint shown when developers mock by instance.

behaviourChanges.title: Mocking hint no longer written to the debug log
behaviourChanges.detail: In the baseline, setMock(fflib_ISObjectSelector) and setMock(fflib_ISObjectDomain) wrote an INFO-level debug message. It warned that the mock must have sObjectType() stubbed, or that the caller should use setMock(SObjectType, mock). The evolved code drops this message. Developers whose mocks return null from sObjectType() now get the mock registered under a null key with no hint, and later see confusing factory errors or real (unmocked) instances. Return values, exceptions, mock registration, sharing, limits and null handling are unchanged. The debug log is very slightly smaller. These methods are @TestVisible and protected, so in practice this only affects test-time diagnostics.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: No functional assertion can observe debug output. Instead, add a test that calls Selector.setMock and Domain.setMock with a mock whose sObjectType() returns null, and pin the resulting behaviour: either a DeveloperException, or that newInstance(Account.SObjectType) does not return the mock. That way the case the hint warned about is defined by a test.

patterns.title: Clearing PMD findings by deleting side-effect-only debug statements
patterns.detail: Deleting debug statements that only print hints is a reasonable way to satisfy AvoidDebugStatements without suppressions, and it cannot change control flow. The trade-off is lost developer guidance. Moving the hint into the ApexDoc on both overloads, or validating that sObjectType() is not null and throwing a DeveloperException, would keep it in a PMD-clean way.

patterns.title: Treating headroom and run-time deltas as caused by the change
patterns.detail: Iteration 1's learning credits the deletion with 'slightly raised the speed and headroom scores'. The headroom test never reaches setMock, and later iterations show headroom moving by up to 6.5 points with no relevant change. So the scores are noisy within about the 5-point margin, and the learning recorded for future climbs is misleading.
patterns.evidence: fflib_ApplicationTest.cls:581-614 (no setMock calls); iterations 2-4 deltas of -4.1, -2.5, -6.5

patterns.title: Discarding micro-optimisations in the selectById and ServiceFactory hot paths
patterns.detail: Iterations 2 to 4 would have changed selectById, selectByRelationship and ServiceFactory.newInstance. All were discarded, so the null filtering, the mixed-SObjectType validation and the containsKey-based mock lookup in the baseline are kept. That is the safe outcome: iteration 2's get() != null lookup, for example, would have treated a service mock registered as null differently.

testGaps.title: Mock registered by instance with unstubbed sObjectType()
testGaps.detail: No test covers setMock(instance) where sObjectType() returns null. This was the scenario the deleted hint warned about, and its behaviour is currently undefined by tests.
testGaps.proposedTest: Register a selector mock and a domain mock whose sObjectType() returns null via Selector.setMock and Domain.setMock. Assert what newInstance(Account.SObjectType) returns (the real implementation, not the mock), or assert a DeveloperException if validation is added.

testGaps.title: Headroom test does not exercise mock paths
testGaps.detail: headroomBulkFactoryCalls only uses real factories. Mock registration and lookup (m_sObjectByMock..., m_serviceInterfaceTypeByMockService) are not measured, so headroom cannot detect regressions or gains in setMock and its lookups.
testGaps.proposedTest: Add a headroom variant that registers selector, domain and service mocks once. Then call newInstance and selectById in the same bulk loop, and assert that the mocks are returned on every call.

testGaps.title: Service mock registered as null
testGaps.detail: ServiceFactory.newInstance uses containsKey, so a mock explicitly registered as null returns null. Nothing pins this, and the discarded iteration 2 would have silently changed it to return the real implementation.
testGaps.proposedTest: Call Service.setMock(IAccountService.class, null) and assert that Service.newInstance(IAccountService.class) returns null. Or decide it should throw, and assert that instead.

other.title: Coverage being flat depends on how the scorer counts lines
other.detail: The plan predicted 109/121 going to 107/119 (about 89.9%). The score stayed at 90.1, which implies each multi-line System.debug statement counts as one line, or the rounding absorbed it. This was a zero-margin dimension, so the keep came close to failing.

other.title: Scores are too noisy for CPU micro-optimisations
other.detail: Headroom varies by about ±6 points between runs, which is comparable to the 5-point margin. Future ascents on this class should repeat headroom measurements or raise rounds before judging CPU edits. The 'learnings' from iterations 2 to 4 (native copy is cheaper than a loop, string ops cost more than describe calls) may also reflect noise rather than real cost differences.
